arxiv-2306-13164.description: Abstract We investigate the effect of localization on the local charging of quantum batteries (QBs) modeled by disordered spin systems. arxiv-2401-14965.title: An Improved Lower Bound on Oblivious Transfer Capacity via Interactive Erasure Emulation
arxiv-2401-14965.creator: So Suda, Shun Watanabe, and Haruya Yamaguchi
arxiv-2401-14965.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by So Suda, Shun Watanabe, and Haruya Yamaguchi. We revisit the oblivious transfer (OT) capacities of noisy channels against the passive adversary, which have been identified only for a limited class of channels. In the literature, the general construction of oblivious transfer has been known only for generalized erasure channels (GECs); for other channels, we first convert a given channel to a GEC via alphabet extension and erasure emulation, and then apply the general construction for GEC.

arxiv-2402-10052.title: UnDIAL : Self-Distillation with Adjusted Logits for Robust Unlearning in Large Language Models
arxiv-2402-10052.creator: Yijiang River Dong, Hongzhou Lin, Mikhail Belkin, Ramon Huerta, Ivan Vulic
arxiv-2402-10052.description: Abstract Mitigating the retention of sensitive or private information in large language models is essential for enhancing privacy and safety. Existing unlearning methods, like Gradient Ascent and Negative Preference Optimization, directly tune models to remove unwanted information. However, these methods often become unstable because they fine-tune by maximizing cross-entropy loss, which is the opposite of traditional loss minimization in learning.

arxiv-2509-14278.title: Beyond Data Privacy: New Privacy Risks for Large Language Models
arxiv-2509-14278.creator: Yuntao Du, Zitao Li, Ninghui Li, Bolin Ding † \dagger Department of Computer Science, Purdue University {ytdu, ninghui}@purdue.edu ‡ \ddagger Alibaba {zitao.l, bolin.ding}@alibaba-inc.com
arxiv-2509-14278.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in natural language understanding, reasoning, and autonomous decision-making. However, these advancements have also come with significant privacy concerns. While significant research has focused on mitigating the data privacy risks of LLMs during various stages of model training, less attention has been paid to new threats emerging from their deployment.
